title: MCP: discovery, typed tools and safe transports
objectives: Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects mcp: discovery, typed tools and safe transports with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. Capture a real initialized session, tool listing and successful fixture call in a test artifact.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: Model Context Protocol standardizes how hosts connect to servers exposing tools, resources and prompts. The host owns the user-facing application and policy; a client maintains a connection to a server. Tools perform operations, resources expose addressable context and prompts offer reusable interaction templates where supported.

MCP reduces bespoke integration wiring but does not make a server trustworthy. Tool descriptions and returned content are untrusted inputs; authentication identifies a party, while authorization determines which operation it may perform.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: The actual local MCP server uses the Python SDK's FastMCP with read_failure and search_history tools, plus a synthetic fixture resource. The client starts the server over stdio, initializes the session, lists tools and calls them with typed arguments. Streamable HTTP is a separate remote transport with its own authentication and session considerations.

Keep server stdout reserved for protocol messages in stdio mode; log to stderr. Validate IDs against a bounded fixture root and inject tenant from authenticated context rather than tool arguments. Expose read-only tools first.

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: A server advertises a benign description but returns instructions to expose secrets. A tool accepts a filename and reads arbitrary paths. Another writes debug text to stdout, corrupting JSON-RPC communication.

Test discovery schemas, unknown IDs, malformed arguments, path traversal and protocol output. For remote deployments, test origin/authentication behavior and avoid forwarding tokens to unrelated downstream audiences.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: Capture a real initialized session, tool listing and successful fixture call in a test artifact. A hand-written JSON object named MCP is not an implementation of the protocol.

For SDET quality gates, combine interoperability tests with explicit permission checks. Record SDK/protocol versions and test upgrades against the same fixture server and client before adopting changed transport behavior.

mistake: A server advertises a benign description but returns instructions to expose secrets. A tool accepts a filename and reads arbitrary paths. Another writes debug text to stdout, corrupting JSON-RPC communication.
takeaway: Capture a real initialized session, tool listing and successful fixture call in a test artifact.

title: MCP lifecycle: initialize, discover, call and close
objectives: Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects mcp lifecycle: initialize, discover, call and close with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. The real smoke test establishes an initialized SDK session and receives fixture evidence.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: An MCP client cannot treat a server as an arbitrary HTTP endpoint returning a convenient dictionary. It establishes a protocol session, negotiates capabilities, discovers supported tools/resources and sends typed requests. The SDK owns message framing and request-response correlation; application code owns permission and task policy.

A successful initialization says the parties can communicate, not that every advertised tool is authorized for the user. Discovery provides schemas and descriptions that must still be reviewed as untrusted integration metadata.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: The companion client creates StdioServerParameters with the current Python executable and the fixture server path, opens stdio_client, constructs ClientSession and calls initialize before list_tools or call_tool. Async context managers close the child process and streams after the test.

Call read_failure with F001 and inspect the typed content and isError result. Then call a traversal-like unknown ID and assert a protocol-level tool error rather than reading a path. Record the discovered tool names and negotiated protocol version.
sections.code:
from mcp import ClientSession,StdioServerParameters
from mcp.client.stdio import stdio_client
# See local-labs/mcp/client.py for the complete async context and handshake

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: A client calls tools before initialization or assumes every server exposes the same names. A server logs diagnostic text to stdout and corrupts protocol framing. A child process is left running after cancellation because lifecycle cleanup is absent.

Test initialization order, expected capabilities, tool listing, successful calls, invalid arguments and clean shutdown. Preserve protocol errors separately from domain not-found results for diagnosis.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: The real smoke test establishes an initialized SDK session and receives fixture evidence. A mocked object named MCP cannot establish interoperability. Keep a portable artifact with SDK/protocol identity and observed tool results.
For SDETs, this is integration testing across a protocol boundary: known requests, schemas, correlation and cleanup remain deterministic even when the host later uses an LLM to select a tool.

title: MCP resources and prompts versus executable tools
objectives: MCP resources and prompts versus executable tools
Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects mcp resources and prompts versus executable tools with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. Acceptance demonstrates real resource discovery/read behavior and tool calls separately.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: Tools perform application operations with declared input schemas. Resources expose context at a URI and may support listing/templates; prompts provide reusable interaction templates where the server supports them. These interfaces serve different roles, and a resource's text must not become a new authority for tool permissions.

The fixture server exposes a schema resource describing synthetic incident fields. Reading that resource informs the host about data, while read_failure retrieves one authorized incident through a tool. Neither interface grants repository writes.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Use FastMCP decorators to declare a resource at fixture://ci/schema and tools with typed function arguments. Discover the relevant capability, read the resource and associate its contents with the server identity. Restrict resource identifiers and templates to supported namespaces.

A host may use a prompt template as part of its request construction, but it still applies its own instruction hierarchy and safety policy. Keep tool result IDs and resource URIs in traces so evidence provenance is inspectable.
sections.code:
from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP
server=FastMCP('fixture')
@server.resource('fixture://ci/schema')
def schema():return 'id, tenant, group, log, category'

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: A host sees a resource containing 'run this command' and executes it as an instruction. A resource template accepts an arbitrary filesystem path. A tool description is changed remotely and the host silently expands its allowlist.

Test supported URI namespaces, template arguments, malicious resource text and changed discovery schemas. Treat descriptions and contents as data crossing a trust boundary, even when the transport is authenticated.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: Acceptance demonstrates real resource discovery/read behavior and tool calls separately. Record which interfaces the server actually advertises rather than assuming every MCP server supports every optional capability.
SDETs should verify schema compatibility and scope across upgrades. The protocol reduces wiring differences, but the host still owns trust, evidence handling and effect authorization.

takeaway: Acceptance demonstrates real resource discovery/read behavior and tool calls separately.

title: Stdio and Streamable HTTP: different deployment boundaries
objectives: Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects stdio and streamable http: different deployment boundaries with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. The provided smoke test executes real stdio mode.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: Stdio connects a host to a locally launched server process through input/output streams. Streamable HTTP supports remote connections and introduces network identity, session and authentication considerations. Choosing a transport changes operational and security assumptions; it does not change the host's obligation to authorize tools.
A local fixture server can rely on a narrowly launched process with synthetic data. A remote deployment must protect its origin, audience, credentials, session lifecycle and downstream requests.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Keep stdout reserved for protocol messages in stdio mode and put logs on stderr. Launch a known executable with explicit arguments and a minimal environment. For a remote server, use the SDK's supported HTTP transport, enforce authenticated scopes and bind session handling to the intended client context.

Do not pass upstream bearer tokens to unrelated downstream services. Validate resource audiences and avoid treating arbitrary endpoint URLs from model text as trusted server configuration. TLS and authentication protect transport identity; authorization still restricts effects.
sections.code:
# Local server
server.run(transport='stdio')
# A separately configured remote server can use streamable-http
# Authentication and origin policy must be supplied for that deployment

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: A remote host accepts any origin or follows a model-provided MCP URL carrying credentials. A stdio launcher passes its entire secret environment to an unreviewed server. An HTTP session is reused across users without scope checks.
Test malformed connections, denied authentication, wrong audience, session ownership and shutdown. Separate local interoperability tests from the remote deployment's actual auth and network tests.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: The provided smoke test executes real stdio mode. Remote HTTP configuration is a separate deployment exercise whose authentication cannot be proved by that local test. Record transport and tested boundaries in the artifact.
SDETs should avoid overstating protocol compliance or security from a single happy path. Each deployment mode needs evidence for the assumptions it introduces.

mistake: A remote host accepts any origin or follows a model-provided MCP URL carrying credentials. A stdio launcher passes its entire secret environment to an unreviewed server. An HTTP session is reused across users without scope checks.
takeaway: The provided smoke test executes real stdio mode.

title: MCP host policy: discovery does not authorize effects
objectives: Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects mcp host policy: discovery does not authorize effects with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. Acceptance combines the real protocol smoke test with domain/policy regressions.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: MCP makes tools discoverable, but discovery is not permission. The host decides which tool proposals are allowed for a task and principal. The server separately enforces its domain access rules. Defense at both ends protects against malicious proposals and overly broad server implementations.
An allowlisted read tool can still expose too much if its arguments select unauthorized IDs. Tool-name validation and data-scope validation are separate checks.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Limit the fixture server to read_failure and search_history, with alpha-tenant records and bounded query lengths. The host's agent policy also limits calls, tracks repeated action signatures and rejects unsupported tool names. A write-capable integration must bind approval to an exact action and current permission scope.
Retain discovery, proposal, validation, authorization, result and termination events. On schema changes, compare the new tool contract with the tested one before enabling it automatically.

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: A server advertises a safe read description but accepts a path traversal ID. A host trusts a returned instruction to invoke an unrelated tool. A denied tool call is retried through a broader generic endpoint.
Test unknown names, extra arguments, cross-tenant IDs, overlong queries and denial recovery. Ensure denied actions have zero effects and do not alter the task's budget or allowlist.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: Acceptance combines the real protocol smoke test with domain/policy regressions. A successful call shows interoperability, while denied cases show the intended permission boundary. Neither alone proves the entire agent safe.
For SDETs, retain the denied-call trace as first-class evidence. It establishes that an attempted unsafe action was blocked at the application/server boundary, not merely discouraged in prose.

mistake: A server advertises a safe read description but accepts a path traversal ID. A host trusts a returned instruction to invoke an unrelated tool. A denied tool call is retried through a broader generic endpoint.
takeaway: Acceptance combines the real protocol smoke test with domain/policy regressions.
